Findings:

- (a) Isolation is real, traced end to end. store.ex:199 write_v2/2 calls write_status(path, ...) on BOTH branches (success line 208, refusal line 203); write_status (store.ex:364) writes to status_path/1 (store.ex:371) = Path.join(Path.dirname(artifact_path), "last_run.status"). Old path was <tmp>/store_load_N.coverdata, so dirname = System.tmp_dir!() and the sidecar was literally <tmp>/last_run.status - machine-global. New path is <tmp>/store_load_<ospid>_<12hex>/per_test.coverdata (store_test.exs:409-413), so dirname is the test-private dir. Verified empirically, not just by reading: ran the file with TMPDIR pointed at a clean scratch root; afterwards the root contained only Mix's own mix_lock/mix_pubsub entries and NO last_run.status. 30 tests, 0 failures.

- (a2) The old on_exit was the destructive half of the bug, and it is gone. It ran File.rm_rf!(Path.join(Path.dirname(tmp_path), "last_run.status")) - i.e. it deleted <tmp>/last_run.status, a path this test never owned. Any concurrent VM's sidecar was fair game. The new cleanup cannot touch anything outside its own directory.

- (b) refute File.exists?(path) at store_test.exs:438 still holds and still means what it did. File.mkdir_p!(tmp_dir) at :412 creates the directory only; path is a distinct child name (per_test.coverdata) that nothing writes, so the refute is false-for-the-original-reason (no coverdata artifact), not vacuously true for a new one. Note the near-miss that did NOT happen: File.exists?/1 returns true for directories, so had the setup handed back tmp_dir itself as :path this assertion would have started FAILING loudly rather than passing silently. It is arguably now stronger than before - the old flat name used a VM-local counter in a shared root where a stale leftover from a killed run could in principle already occupy it; the new root carries os-pid plus 48 CSPRNG bits.

- (c) There are TWO such calls in the load/1 describe, not three: store_test.exs:450 and :459. (The third the mandate may be counting is :389 in the read_status/1 describe - different block, untouched.) Both are UNCHANGED IN MEANING, not merely "still idempotent". They were already no-ops before this diff: the old Path.dirname(path) was System.tmp_dir!(), and System.tmp_dir!/0 by contract returns an existing writable directory (it raises otherwise), so mkdir_p! never had anything to create there either. Before and after, they are redundant-but-harmless precondition documentation. Nothing those two tests exercised has been lost; they still write raw bytes to path and assert Store.load/1 classifies them :invalid_artifact.

- (d) No test body was changed. git diff <base>..HEAD is 1 file, +11/-6, and every changed line sits inside the setup do ... end block at store_test.exs:403-418. Mandate honored.

- (e) Cleanup is correct and leak-free, and cannot race. on_exit(fn -> File.rm_rf!(tmp_dir) end) removes exactly the tree setup created, including both the coverdata and the sidecar. setup (not setup_all) runs per test, and each run mints a fresh cross_vm_suffix/0 = "#{System.pid()}_#{12 hex}" (temp_name.ex:19), so no two tests in the module can be handed the same tmp_dir - intra-module racing is impossible by construction. ETC-ISO-005 is satisfied: the closure captures only a plain binary, so it needs no test-process state from the separate on_exit process.

- (f) async: true (store_test.exs:2) is now honest for this block; it was not before. Within the module the old exposure was narrow (only :430 calls write_v2 in this block, and the read_status/1 and v2-round-trip blocks already had private dirs). The real exposure was machine-level: <tmp>/last_run.status is a fixed name shared with every other BEAM on the host - including a nested `mix spec.check` merged run executing tests inside a specled run - and the old on_exit deleted it unconditionally. That whole surface is closed.

- (g) Clean. No Process.sleep, no spawn/Task/Agent/unmanaged processes anywhere in the file (grep for spawn|Task.|Process.|Agent.|start_supervised returns nothing; record/2 merely stores self() as data). The read_status/1 block's claim of being already private checks out - store_test.exs:335-341 allocates its own dir and parks the artifact inside it, so its sidecar is private too. Remaining shared-tmp roots use System.unique_integer/1 (:60, :86, :99, :161, :239, :336) and are therefore only VM-local unique. That is NOT a defect here: specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach explicitly designates System.unique_integer/1-named test roots under System.tmp_dir!() as ACCEPTED RISK, with the carve-out limited to tests that File.ls! a shared root or glob-delete sweep it. Neither pattern appears in this file (no File.ls!, no Path.wildcard; every rm_rf! targets one specific allocated path), so the sibling blocks sit inside the accepted-risk envelope. The diff's use of cross_vm_suffix/0 is the correct call under the same ADR's "new tests that allocate shared-tmp roots should reach for cross_vm_suffix/0" clause - this setup allocates a root that did not previously exist, so the cited justification is honest rather than decorative.

- Housekeeping: mix format --check-formatted passes on the file. mix test test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs passes (30 tests, 0 failures) on two seeds, including the isolated-TMPDIR run.
